Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Digital revenue collection exists via NamRA/ITAS (integrated tax system for electronic filing; PAYE returns expected to be lodged online through ITAS, per description of ITAS rollout).[HRTorQue (re ITAS operational 2019)](https://hrtorque.co.za/namibia-implementation-of-integrated-tax-system/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. NamRA's own tax payments brochure confirms EFT, direct deposit and point-of-sale payments (alongside cash) are accepted for all tax types, and the ITAS portal (itas.namra.org.na) provides 24/7 online filing and payment self-service. The original single hrtorque.co.za blog (2019) was a weak source but the underlying finding holds; 'Yes' (3) retained on the strength of NamRA's own documentation.

revision_notes: Confirmed. Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border integration to PAPSS appears planned/being pursued; Afreximbank is hoping to integrate Namibia into PAPSS (not yet live).[The Namibian](https://www.namibian.com.na/namibia-can-benefit-from-africa-trade-payment-system/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Updated. As of March 2026, Namclear (Namibia's payment clearing house) signed an agreement with PayInc to connect to the SADC TCIB regional instant cross-border payment system; system integration is reported complete and the service is being introduced in phases for low-value push payments to South Africa and other Common Monetary Area countries, though settlement remains deferred and end-user rollout was not yet confirmed live. Namibia's separate PAPSS membership remains unconfirmed as of July 2026 (Afreximbank was still urging central banks, including presumably Namibia's, to join). Revised from 'Planned' (2) to 'Under development' (3) given the signed, technically-integrated but not-yet-fully-live cross-border linkage.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: G2P instant payments are being rolled out but not yet at national scale: IPS/IPP initial use case is Government-to-Person (social grants/pensions) and currently in UAT/pilots for banked beneficiaries.[New Era](https://neweralive.na/namibia-draws-closer-to-instant-government-payments/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated with fresher sources. Namibia's Instant Payment System, publicly branded 'WayaMe', completed its G2P pilot in mid-2026 with banked social grant beneficiaries via Bank Windhoek, Letshego Bank Namibia and NamPost, and is being rolled out in phases with G2P (social grants) as phase one, targeted for Q3 2026. This had not reached active, national-scale G2P use at the time of research. 'Limited Use' (2) retained.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Namibia’s Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 includes consumer protection provisions for electronic transactions and requires suppliers to provide secure/transparent payment systems (general e-commerce consumer protections rather than payments-system specific).[ITLawCo – Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019](https://itlawco.com/focus-areas/it-law/electronic-transactions-act-4-of-2019-namibia/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded. Namibia's Payment System Management Act 2023 (Act 14 of 2023) contains a dedicated Part 8 'Consumer Protection' (fee transparency, disclosure, complaints, data sharing principles), and Bank of Namibia payment system determinations PSD-1 (licensing, effective 2024) and a 2025/26 determination on fees/basic bank accounts each contain explicit payment-specific consumer protection clauses, including a prohibition on charging customers for erroneous transactions with mandatory reversal within 14 days and defined complaint-handling timelines. This is dedicated, payment-specific consumer protection regulation going well beyond the general Electronic Transactions Act 2019 originally cited. Revised from 'Partial' (2) to 'Yes' (3).

revision_notes: Upgraded. Revised from 'Ad Hoc' (2) to 'Monthly/Quarterly' (4).

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: Refugee access exists at least via humanitarian cash assistance delivered through mobile money: UNHCR cash-based interventions in Namibia were facilitated by MTC Namibia mobile money service for refugees/asylum-seekers (~6,000 individuals in Osire settlement).[UN Namibia (UNHCR article)](https://namibia.un.org/en/289948-cash-based-interventions-provide-ray-hope-refugees-namibia-amid-severe-drought-and-funding
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated. FNB Namibia launched formal banking services (mobile app, USSD and Cashplus agent cardless deposits/withdrawals) at Osire refugee settlement in September 2025 for around 3,000 previously unbanked adults who held refugee IDs/passports, in addition to the pre-existing UNHCR/MTC Maris mobile-money cash-assistance channel serving roughly 6,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. Access remains partial rather than full: it is settlement-specific, still dependent on refugees holding recognised documentation, and 2025 reporting notes some registered refugees were excluded from cash assistance due to funding constraints. 'Partial' (2) retained.
